q: Elevator 基础需求包含哪些约束？（多选）
q_en: Which constraints are part of the base Elevator problem? (Select all that apply)
options: 需要实现载重、门控和紧急停止
用户可发 hall call，进入后可选目的楼层
仿真通过 step/tick 离散推进
3 部电梯服务 0-9 共 10 层
why: 基础题聚焦调度和移动模拟。载重、门、紧急停止、动态配置和 UI 都被排除。
why_en: The base elevator design focuses on three elevators, ten floors, hall and destination requests, and discrete simulation ticks.
options_en: The system must implement weight limits, door control, and emergency stop.
Users can send a hall call, and once inside pick a destination floor.
The simulation advances through discrete step/tick calls.
Three elevators serve ten floors, numbered 0 through 9.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推进仿真一个离散时间单位的方法调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: step() advances the discrete-time simulation by one tick.

optionExplanations: 载重、门控、紧急停止是真实电梯的硬件安全层，这道题只做调度仿真，不建这些部件。
hall call 加轿厢内选楼层，是整个仿真唯一的请求入口，没它就没有 pickup/destination 可调度。
把时间切成离散 tick，每次 step 只推进一步，仿真行为可预测、可复现。
3 部电梯、10 层楼把规模钉死，楼层合法性和电梯数量从一开始就有明确边界。
optionExplanations_en: Weight limits, door control, and emergency stop are hardware-safety concerns for a real elevator, but this scoped design only simulates scheduling and movement.
A hall call plus an in-cab floor pick is the only request entry point driving the simulation — without it there's nothing to schedule.
Slicing time into discrete ticks means each step advances exactly one unit, keeping the simulation predictable and reproducible.
Fixing three elevators and ten floors pins the scale, so valid-floor and elevator-count boundaries are clear from the start.

q_en: What are the core entities in the Elevator design?
options: ElevatorController、Elevator、Request
Floor、Door、Sensor
Passenger、Payment、Ticket
Building、Lobby、Renderer
why: Controller 负责任务分配和 step 推进，Elevator 管自身位置、方向和请求集合，Request 捕获楼层和类型。Floor 只是整数。
why_en: The core model is a controller coordinating elevators, each elevator owning movement state, and requests carrying floor and type.

  ElevatorController --> Request

options_en: ElevatorController, Elevator, and Request.
Floor, Door, and Sensor.
Passenger, Payment, and Ticket.
Building, Lobby, and Renderer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

optionExplanations: 这三类刚好覆盖调度协调、单梯运动状态和请求身份三件事，是这道题真正要建的模型。
楼层、门和传感器属于硬件控制层，这道题范围内没有门控和传感器，不需要为它们建类。
乘客、计费、票据是电商或购票系统的实体，跟电梯调度和移动无关。
楼宇外壳和渲染层是 UI/物理呈现，这道题只考调度逻辑，不建这些展示层对象。
optionExplanations_en: These three classes are exactly enough to cover fleet coordination, one elevator's motion state, and request identity.
Floor, door, and sensor are hardware-control concerns, and this problem's scope has no door control or sensors to model.
Passenger, payment, and ticket are entities from a booking or billing system, unrelated to elevator scheduling.
Building shell and renderer are UI or physical-presentation concerns; this problem only covers scheduling logic.

scenario: 需求中楼层只表示位置，没有状态、规则或生命周期。
scenario_en: In scope, a floor is only a position; it has no state, rules, or lifecycle.
q: Floor 应该如何建模？
q_en: How should Floor be modeled?
options: 包含乘客队列和门状态的类
int 楼层号
Elevator 的子类
RequestType 枚举值
why: 当前范围里 floor 不维护任何状态，只是坐标。把它建成类会增加无用间接层。
why_en: Floor remains an integer because it has no state or behavior in the scoped problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果后续要建模楼层按钮、显示屏、门厅传感器或无障碍区域，Floor 才可能成为实体。
options_en: A class holding a passenger queue and door state.
A plain int floor number.
A subclass of Elevator.
A RequestType enum value.
tradeoff: int 原语 vs 独立 Floor 类

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

optionExplanations: 楼层要真的管乘客队列和门状态时才值得建类，本题范围没有门控，这个类会是空壳。
本题里楼层只是坐标，没有状态或行为，用 int 就够，也让 Request 和 Elevator 直接持有它。
楼层不是电梯的特化版本，继承关系在语义上就错了。
RequestType 表达的是请求种类，把位置塞进枚举会把楼层和请求类型混成一件事。
optionExplanations_en: A Floor class earns its keep only once it owns a passenger queue or door state; in this scope it would stay an empty shell.
Floor is nothing but a coordinate here, so a plain int is enough and lets Request or Elevator hold it directly.
A floor isn't a specialized elevator, so an inheritance relationship is semantically wrong.
RequestType encodes the kind of request, not a location — folding floor into it conflates two different things.

q: RequestType 需要区分哪些类型？（多选）
q_en: Which request types does RequestType need to distinguish? (Select all that apply)
options: PICKUP_UP
IDLE
DESTINATION
PICKUP_DOWN
why: hall call 有方向，destination 是轿厢内按钮，不带方向。IDLE 属于 Elevator 的 Direction，不是请求类型。
why_en: RequestType distinguishes up pickups, down pickups, and destination stops, while IDLE belongs to elevator direction.
options_en: PICKUP_UP for an up hall call.
IDLE for no active request.
DESTINATION for an in-cab floor button.
PICKUP_DOWN for a down hall call.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了上行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_UP is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the up button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了下行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_DOWN is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the down button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轿厢内乘客按下的目的楼层请求，不带方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DESTINATION is an in-cab floor request that carries no direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

optionExplanations: 楼层外呼叫必须带方向，PICKUP_UP 让向上电梯才去接这个人。
IDLE 描述的是电梯自己有没有请求、要不要动，属于 Direction 而不是请求种类。
轿厢内按下的目的楼层不带方向，到达即服务，所以单独算一种类型。
同理，PICKUP_DOWN 让下行电梯去接，不会被上行电梯错误接走。
optionExplanations_en: A hall call needs a direction, and PICKUP_UP makes sure only an up-moving elevator answers it.
IDLE describes whether the elevator itself has work to do, so it belongs to Direction, not to request type.
An in-cab destination has no direction — the elevator just serves it on arrival, so it gets its own type.
Symmetrically, PICKUP_DOWN routes the pickup to a down-moving elevator instead of an upward one.

scenario: 电梯在 5 楼向上，已有 7、8 楼请求；7 楼有人按 DOWN。
scenario_en: The elevator is on floor 5 moving up with requests at floors 7 and 8; someone on floor 7 presses DOWN.
q: 为什么只用 Set<Integer> 存楼层不够？
q_en: Why is Set<Integer> not enough for pending floors?
options: 楼层号不能比较大小
Set<Integer> 不能去重
无法区分 7 楼向上停靠和 7 楼向下接人
目的楼层不能用整数表示
why: 同一楼层不同请求类型语义不同。向上的电梯不应为了 PICKUP_DOWN 在 7 楼停下接错方向乘客。
why_en: A floor-only request loses whether a hall call is for up or down pickup.
whenOtherWins: 初级或极简模拟可以只存楼层，只要承认会有方向体验问题。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  F["floor 7"] --> U["PICKUP_UP"]
  F --> D["PICKUP_DOWN"]
  U --> A["up elevator may stop"]
  D --> B["down elevator may stop"]
options_en: Floor numbers cannot be compared for ordering.
Set<Integer> cannot deduplicate entries.
It cannot distinguish an up-bound stop at floor 7 from a down pickup at floor 7.
A destination floor cannot be represented as an integer.
tradeoff: Set<Integer> vs Set<Request>

termDefinitions.meaning: 只存楼层号的集合，无法区分同楼层不同方向的请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Set<Integer> stores only floor numbers and cannot distinguish same-floor requests of different direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储 Request 对象的集合，用楼层加类型共同判重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Set<Request> stores Request objects and de-duplicates using floor plus type together.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了上行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_UP is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the up button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了下行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_DOWN is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the down button on a floor.

optionExplanations: 整数天然可比较大小，排序和距离计算都没问题，这不是失败点。
Set 恰恰会去重——问题在于它把 7 楼两个不同方向的请求错误合并成一个。
同一楼层的上行停靠和下行接人是两件事，只存楼层号会把它们混成一条记录。
目的楼层照样能用整数表示，这不是本题真正的限制。
optionExplanations_en: Integers compare fine for ordering and distance, so that isn't the actual failure.
A Set does deduplicate — the real issue is it wrongly merges two different-direction requests at floor 7 into one.
An up-bound stop and a down pickup at the same floor 7 are two different things a floor-only entry can't tell apart.
A destination floor is still perfectly representable as an integer, so that isn't the real limitation.

why: 同楼层不同方向不能被 Set 合并成一个请求。目的楼层则可在任何方向停靠。
why_en: Request equality should include both floor and request type so opposite-direction hall calls remain distinct.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了下行按钮。

scenario: 电梯没有任何请求时，不应该继续向上或向下漂移。
scenario_en: When an elevator has no pending requests, it should not keep drifting up or down.
q: Direction enum 为什么需要 IDLE？
q_en: Why does the Direction enum need IDLE?
options: 表示电梯故障
表示 hall call 的向上按钮
表示目的楼层
表示无请求不移动的状态
why: UP/DOWN 只能表示运动方向，不能表达静止。IDLE 让 step 在无请求时自然停住。
why_en: IDLE represents an elevator with no active movement, preventing it from drifting forever.
whenOtherWins: 如果用 nullable direction 或状态机对象，也能表达 idle，但 enum 更简单。
options_en: It represents an elevator malfunction.
It represents the up button of a hall call.
It represents a destination floor.
It represents the no-requests, not-moving state.
tradeoff: IDLE 枚举值 vs nullable direction

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

optionExplanations: 故障应该用单独的错误状态或字段表达，混进 Direction 会让正常和异常判断纠缠。
上行按钮的方向属于 hall call 的 RequestType，不该塞进电梯自身的运动方向。
目的楼层是 Request 里的一个字段，不是电梯的运动方向。
UP/DOWN 只能表达在动，电梯没请求时需要一个显式的静止值，否则 step 无法收敛。
optionExplanations_en: A malfunction deserves its own error state or field — folding it into Direction blurs normal and abnormal cases.
The up-button direction belongs to the hall call's RequestType, not to the elevator's own movement state.
A destination floor is a field on Request, not a direction the elevator moves in.
UP/DOWN can only describe motion, so an elevator with no requests needs an explicit still value or step never settles.

q_en: Which state should an Elevator store? (Select all that apply)
options: currentFloor
direction
其他电梯的位置
requests: Set<Request>
why: 单部电梯只管理自身运动。其他电梯由 ElevatorController 观察和调度。
why_en: An Elevator owns its current floor, direction, and pending requests, not the whole fleet.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class Elevator
  class ElevatorController
  class Request
  ElevatorController --> Elevator
  Elevator --> Request
  Request : floor
  Request : type
options_en: currentFloor, its own position.
direction, its own movement state.
The positions of other elevators.
requests: Set<Request>, its own pending stops.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储 Request 对象的集合，用楼层加类型共同判重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Set<Request> stores Request objects and de-duplicates using floor plus type together.

optionExplanations: 每次移动和边界检查都要知道自己在哪层，这是最基本的状态。
UP/DOWN/IDLE 决定该不该反向、该不该停，缺了它 step 无法判断下一步。
全局视图属于 Controller 的职责，单部电梯知道别的电梯位置会打破封装边界。
自己的待服务请求集合决定它下一步往哪走、在哪停，是这台电梯的核心待办清单。
optionExplanations_en: Every movement and boundary check needs to know which floor it's on right now — the most basic piece of state.
UP/DOWN/IDLE decides whether to reverse or stop, so step can't make its next move without it.
Fleet-wide visibility is the controller's job; letting one elevator know others' positions breaks encapsulation.
Its own pending-request set is what decides where it heads next and where it stops — this elevator's to-do list.

scenario: 用户在 5 楼按上行按钮，系统需要决定哪部电梯响应。
scenario_en: A user on floor 5 presses the up button, and the system must decide which elevator responds.
q: 这个决策应该放在哪里？
q_en: Where should this dispatch decision live?
options: ElevatorController
单个 Elevator 内部逻辑
Request 的构造函数中
Floor 这个类里
why: 调度需要看多部电梯的全局状态，因此属于 Controller。单个 Elevator 不应该知道其他电梯。
why_en: Dispatch belongs in ElevatorController because it requires fleet-level information.
whenOtherWins: 单电梯系统可以直接给该 Elevator.addRequest，省掉 Controller 调度逻辑。
options_en: ElevatorController.
Inside a single Elevator's own logic.
Inside the Request constructor.
Inside the Floor class.
tradeoff: 全局调度决策 vs 单电梯本地状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装一次停靠请求的类，包含楼层号和请求类型两个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Request object bundles a floor number together with a request type.

optionExplanations: 派发要比较所有电梯的状态才能选出最合适的一部，只有 Controller 拿得到这个全局视角。
单部电梯只认识自己的楼层和请求，让它比较别的电梯会破坏封装边界。
构造函数应该只负责校验和初始化字段，不该在创建对象时顺带做调度决策。
本题没有 Floor 实体，也不该让一个坐标类承担派发这种协调职责。
optionExplanations_en: Dispatch has to compare every elevator's state to pick the best one, and only the controller has that fleet-wide view.
A single elevator only knows its own floor and requests — asking it to compare others breaks the encapsulation boundary.
A constructor should just validate and initialize fields, not sneak in a fleet-wide dispatch decision.
This problem doesn't even model Floor as an entity, and a coordinate class shouldn't own dispatch responsibility.

scenario: requestElevator 是 hall call API，只接受上行或下行呼叫。
scenario_en: requestElevator is the hall-call API, and it accepts only up or down hall calls.
q: 为什么参数用 RequestType 而不是 Direction？
q_en: Why should the API parameter use RequestType instead of Direction?
options: Direction 不能表示上行方向
RequestType 排除 IDLE 值
RequestType 会自动选择电梯
Direction 类型无法做相等比较
why: hall call 不可能是 IDLE。使用更窄的类型减少运行时校验和非法状态。
why_en: Using RequestType for hall calls avoids accepting IDLE as a valid request direction.
whenOtherWins: 内部电梯运动状态仍应使用 Direction，因为它确实需要 IDLE。
options_en: Direction cannot represent the up direction.
RequestType excludes IDLE at the type level.
RequestType automatically selects an elevator.
Direction values cannot be compared for equality.
tradeoff: RequestType 参数 vs Direction 参数

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

optionExplanations: Direction 里明明有 UP，这不是问题所在。
hall call 永远带方向，用 RequestType 能在类型层面就排除 IDLE 这个非法输入，不用运行时再校验。
参数类型只负责表达合法输入，真正选哪部电梯仍由 Controller 的调度逻辑决定。
枚举之间的相等比较没有问题，这不是选类型的理由。
optionExplanations_en: Direction clearly includes UP, so that isn't the actual problem.
A hall call is never IDLE, so typing the parameter as RequestType rules out that illegal value at compile time instead of a runtime check.
The parameter type only shapes valid input — which elevator gets picked is still the controller's dispatch logic.
Enum equality comparisons work fine here; that's not the reason to pick one type over the other.

scenario: 你需要先实现一个简单正确的 dispatch 策略，在小楼轻流量下可接受。
scenario_en: You need a simple, correct dispatch strategy that is acceptable for a small building with light traffic.
q: 最简单策略是什么？
q_en: What is the simplest dispatch strategy?
options: 随机选择任意电梯
总是选择 0 号电梯
选择当前楼层距离请求楼层最近的电梯
只选择当前向下的电梯
why: nearest elevator 容易实现且能工作，但不考虑方向会产生等待体验问题。面试中可先实现再说明局限。
why_en: Nearest-elevator dispatch is simple and acceptable as a first implementation, though it ignores direction.
whenOtherWins: 当体验要求更高时，应考虑方向、当前请求队列是否会经过该楼层、或更完整的调度策略。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["new hall call"] --> B["check elevators"]
  B --> C["score distance and direction"]

whenOtherWins: 如果把请求集合换成有序结构（如按楼层排序的 TreeSet），或本来就不追求可复现的调试仿真，直接用迭代器也能忍受。
optionExplanations: 读取 next() 只是遍历，不会删除任何元素。
requests 非空时，iterator 显然能取到元素，不会为空。
HashSet 遍历顺序不保证稳定，同样的输入两次跑可能选出不同方向，测试和调试都会失灵。
IDLE 本来就要转成 UP 或 DOWN，这不是问题所在。
optionExplanations_en: Calling next() is just a read — it doesn't delete anything from the set.
With requests non-empty, the iterator obviously yields an element; it isn't empty.
HashSet iteration order isn't guaranteed stable, so the same input could pick a different direction on two runs, breaking testing and debugging.
IDLE is supposed to transition into UP or DOWN — that isn't the issue here.

scenario: 电梯在 4 楼向上，6 楼有人按 DOWN，8 楼是 destination。
scenario_en: The elevator is on floor 4 moving up; floor 6 has a DOWN hall call, and floor 8 is a destination.
q: hasRequestsAhead(UP) 应如何看待 6 楼 PICKUP_DOWN？
q_en: How should hasRequestsAhead(UP) treat a PICKUP_DOWN on floor 6?
options: 会被直接从请求集合删除
不算前方请求，电梯应保持 idle 不动
应让电梯立即在 6 楼停靠开门
算前方请求，电梯继续上行但不在 6 楼停
why: travel 和 stop 的条件不同。电梯要朝任何前方请求移动，但只在匹配方向或 destination 停靠。
why_en: Traveling considers any request ahead, while stopping is direction-aware.
whenOtherWins: 如果调度模型规定向上电梯永远不经过反向 pickup，可过滤它，但本文 SCAN 需要经过再回头服务。
options_en: It gets deleted straight from the request set.
It does not count, so the elevator should just stay idle.
It should make the elevator stop immediately at floor 6.
It counts as a request ahead, so the elevator keeps going up but does not stop at floor 6.
tradeoff: travel（朝任意请求移动） vs stop（只为匹配方向停靠）

termDefinitions.meaning: 检查当前方向前方是否还有任意类型的请求，用于决定是否要反向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: hasRequestsAhead checks whether any request exists ahead in the current direction, which drives the reversal decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了下行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_DOWN is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the down button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轿厢内乘客按下的目的楼层请求，不带方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DESTINATION is an in-cab floor request that carries no direction.

optionExplanations: hasRequestsAhead 只是检查，不做任何删除操作。
把它排除在外会让电梯卡在原地，看不到 8 楼那个真正顺路的 destination。
立即停靠会接错方向的乘客，跟 6 楼的 DOWN 请求语义相反。
判断要不要继续走和判断要不要停车用的是两套标准，6 楼的反向请求只影响后者，不影响前者。
optionExplanations_en: hasRequestsAhead only checks; it never removes anything from the set.
Excluding it would strand the elevator in place, blind to the destination at floor 8 that's genuinely ahead.
Stopping immediately would pick up the wrong-direction rider, which is exactly what a DOWN request at floor 6 shouldn't trigger.
Deciding whether to keep moving and deciding whether to stop use different rules — the floor 6 opposite request only affects the second one.

q: 补全 travel 和 stop 的区别：
q_en: Fill in the difference between travel and stop:
text: hasRequestsAhead 检查当前方向前方是否有{{任何请求}}；shouldStopHere 只停 {{同方向 pickup}} 或 {{destination}}。
why: 这个区分解释了为什么电梯会路过反方向 hall call，但稍后反向时接人。
why_en: SCAN travels toward any pending request but stops only for direction-matching pickups or destinations.
tradeoff: travel（朝任意请求移动） vs stop（只为匹配方向停靠）

termDefinitions.meaning: 检查当前方向前方是否还有任意类型的请求，用于决定是否要反向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: hasRequestsAhead checks whether any request exists ahead in the current direction, which drives the reversal decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断电梯是否该在当前楼层停靠的检查，只认同方向 pickup 或 destination。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: shouldStopHere decides whether to stop at the current floor, honoring only same-direction pickups or destinations.

q: 为什么 step 不需要硬编码“到 9 楼就向下、到 0 楼就向上”？
q_en: Why does step not hard-code "go down at 9, go up at 0"?
options: 无前方请求时 hasRequestsAhead 自然触发反向
电梯物理上可以越过 9 楼继续上行
所有请求默认都发生在 0 楼
边界检查由 RequestType 自动完成
why: 方向变化应由请求集合决定，而不是楼层边界硬编码。硬编码可能干扰当前楼层的停靠处理。
why_en: Reversal follows from no requests ahead, so explicit boundary checks are unnecessary and can introduce bugs.
options_en: hasRequestsAhead naturally triggers a reversal once nothing remains ahead.
The elevator can physically travel past floor 9.
Every request is assumed to happen at floor 0.
Boundary checks are handled automatically by RequestType.
tradeoff: 让 hasRequestsAhead 决定反向 vs 硬编码楼层边界

termDefinitions.meaning: 检查当前方向前方是否还有任意类型的请求，用于决定是否要反向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: hasRequestsAhead checks whether any request exists ahead in the current direction, which drives the reversal decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

optionExplanations: 前方没有请求时 hasRequestsAhead 本来就会返回 false，反向逻辑已经自然覆盖了到顶到底的情况。
这道题里楼层是硬边界，电梯不能物理越过 9 楼，这不是理由。
请求可以来自 0-9 任意楼层，默认全在 0 楼这个假设本身就不成立。
RequestType 只区分请求种类，它不知道也不该处理楼层数字边界。
optionExplanations_en: When nothing remains ahead, hasRequestsAhead already returns false, so the reversal logic naturally covers hitting the top or bottom floor.
Floors are a hard boundary in this problem — the elevator can't physically go past floor 9, so that isn't the reason.
Requests can land on any floor 0 through 9, so assuming they're all at floor 0 is simply false.
RequestType only distinguishes kinds of requests; it has no notion of floor-number boundaries at all.

scenario: 请求楼层等于电梯当前楼层，门控 out of scope。
scenario_en: The requested floor equals the elevator current floor, and door behavior is out of scope.
q: addRequest 应如何处理？
q_en: How should addRequest handle this case?
options: 把请求加入集合等待一圈
返回 true，当作已经服务的 no-op
返回 false 表示错误
强制 direction=UP
why: 需求规定当前楼层请求视为已服务。没有门开关模型时，不需要排入请求集合。
why_en: A request for the current floor is treated as already served in the scoped simulation.
whenOtherWins: 如果建模门开关和乘客上下车，可把当前楼层请求转成 open-door action。
options_en: Add it to the request set and let it wait a full loop.
Return true, treating it as a no-op that's already served.
Return false to signal an error.
Force direction to UP.
tradeoff: no-op 直接返回 vs 排入请求队列

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

codeSample:
addRequest(request)
    if request.floor < 0 || request.floor > 9
        return false
    if request.floor == currentFloor
        return true   // already here, no-op
    return requests.add(request)
optionExplanations: 把它排进队列会让一个本已到达的请求多绕一整圈才被处理。
需求把当前楼层请求当作已服务，直接返回 true、不进 requests 集合是最简单的一致实现。
这是一个合法输入，不是错误场景，返回 false 会误报。
强制改方向跟这个请求本身无关，还会破坏电梯原有的运动状态。
optionExplanations_en: Queuing it would make an already-arrived request wait a full extra loop before being handled.
The spec treats a current-floor request as already served, so returning true without touching the request set is the simplest consistent implementation.
This is a legal input, not an error case, so returning false would be a false alarm.
Forcing the direction has nothing to do with this request and would corrupt the elevator's existing motion state.

q: requestElevator / addRequest 应拒绝哪些输入？（多选）
q_en: Which inputs should requestElevator / addRequest reject? (Select all that apply)
options: 楼层小于 0 或大于 9
hall call 使用 DESTINATION 类型
空请求对象
当前楼层 no-op
why: 无效楼层和错误请求类型应拒绝。当前楼层按需求是已服务，不算错误。
why_en: Invalid floors, invalid hall-call types, and null requests should be rejected, while current-floor requests are no-ops.
options_en: A floor number below 0 or above 9.
A hall call that uses the DESTINATION type.
A null request object.
A request for the current floor treated as a no-op.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轿厢内乘客按下的目的楼层请求，不带方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DESTINATION is an in-cab floor request that carries no direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

optionExplanations: 超出 0-9 范围的楼层会让电梯试图停在不存在的地方，必须拒绝。
hall call 只能是 PICKUP_UP/PICKUP_DOWN，用 DESTINATION 冒充楼层外呼叫会破坏方向语义。
没有 floor/type 字段的空对象一旦进入状态机，后续访问就会崩溃，必须提前挡掉。
当前楼层请求按需求视为已服务的 no-op，是合法输入，不该被拒绝。
optionExplanations_en: A floor outside 0–9 would make the elevator try to stop somewhere that doesn't exist, so it must be rejected.
A hall call must be PICKUP_UP or PICKUP_DOWN — letting DESTINATION masquerade as one breaks the direction semantics.
A null object with no floor or type would crash later code that reads those fields, so it needs to be caught early.
A current-floor request is a legitimate no-op that's treated as already served, not something to reject.

scenario: 有人因为 Controller.requestElevator 和 Elevator.addRequest 都“接收请求”而想抽共同接口 IRequestHandler。
scenario_en: Someone wants a shared IRequestHandler interface because Controller.requestElevator and Elevator.addRequest both receive requests.
q: 为什么这是不必要抽象？
q_en: Why is this an unnecessary abstraction?
options: addRequest 其实不能返回 boolean 值
共享接口会导致代码编译失败
语义不同：Controller 协调选择，Elevator 只改队列
requestElevator 根本不需要楼层参数
why: 相同参数形状不代表同一行为。接口应服务可替换多态，而不是为了名字相似。
why_en: Similar method shapes do not justify an interface when the responsibilities are different.
options_en: addRequest cannot actually return a boolean.
A shared interface would fail to compile.
Their semantics differ: the controller coordinates a choice, the elevator only mutates its own queue.
requestElevator does not actually need a floor parameter.
tradeoff: 按行为语义分离接口 vs 按参数形状合并接口

termDefinitions.meaning: 本题中假设的一个公共接口名，用来说明为相似方法签名强行抽公共接口的反例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IRequestHandler is a hypothetical shared interface used here as a counter-example of forcing an interface onto unrelated methods.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

whenOtherWins: 如果未来真的出现多种可互相替换的请求处理器实现，需要在运行时切换，那时抽接口才有实际价值。
optionExplanations: addRequest 完全可以返回 boolean，这不是问题所在。
共享接口在语法上完全能编译通过，编译与否不是判断依据。
选哪部电梯这件事要看多部电梯的状态，addRequest 只是改自己的队列，两者职责不同，硬凑成一个接口没有意义。
这个方法要知道去哪层接人，楼层参数显然是必需的，不能省略。
optionExplanations_en: addRequest can perfectly well return a boolean — that isn't the issue.
A shared interface would compile just fine syntactically, so compilability isn't the deciding factor.
Choosing an elevator has to look across the whole fleet, while addRequest just mutates its own queue — different jobs that don't need forcing into one interface.
requestElevator obviously needs the floor parameter to know which floor to go pick someone up from.

q: 文章中电梯从 3 楼向上服务 5 楼 pickup 和 7 楼 destination 的关键 tick 顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the key tick order from floor 3 to pickup at 5 and destination at 7?
steps: 到 5 楼，移除 PICKUP_UP，并本 tick 不移动。
从 3 楼向上移动到 4 楼。
到 7 楼，移除 DESTINATION，请求清空后 IDLE。
why: 验证展示了停靠消耗 tick、destination 可被服务、请求清空后进入 IDLE。
why_en: The trace validates upward movement, stop ticks, destination handling, and transition to idle.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了上行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_UP is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the up button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轿厢内乘客按下的目的楼层请求，不带方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DESTINATION is an in-cab floor request that carries no direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

scenario: 后续加入 express elevator，只停 0、5、9 层。
scenario_en: A later requirement adds express elevators that stop only at floors 0, 5, and 9.
q: 更好的基础扩展是什么？
q_en: What is the better basic extension?
options: 在 RequestType 里新增 EXPRESS_UP 类型
把所有电梯的请求队列换成 priority queue
直接删掉所有普通（非快速）电梯
给 Elevator 加 isExpress，addRequest 校验楼层
why: express 主要是电梯能力约束和 Controller 的派发偏好，不必改变 Request 结构。
why_en: Express support can be modeled as elevator capability validation plus dispatch preference.
whenOtherWins: 如果有 VIP 或紧急请求，Request 可能需要 priority 字段，但这会影响移动算法。
options_en: Add a new EXPRESS_UP value to RequestType.
Replace every elevator's request queue with a priority queue.
Delete all regular, non-express elevators.
Add isExpress to Elevator and validate allowed floors inside addRequest.
tradeoff: 电梯能力约束 vs 修改 Request 结构

termDefinitions.meaning: 扩展字段，标记某电梯是否为只停靠指定楼层的快速梯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: isExpress is an extension flag marking an elevator that only serves a restricted set of floors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 快速电梯允许停靠的楼层集合，如 {0, 5, 9}。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: expressFloors is the set of floors an express elevator is allowed to serve, such as {0, 5, 9}.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按优先级取出元素的队列，不保证到达顺序或位置顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A priority queue pops elements by priority rather than arrival or positional order.

optionExplanations: 把电梯能力塞进请求类型会让 Request 结构越来越臃肿，跟请求本身语义无关。
换成 priority queue 是给移动排序引入新维度，跟这部电梯只停哪些楼层没关系，还可能打乱 SCAN。
题目要求两种电梯共存，删掉普通电梯会让非快速楼层没人服务。
express 本质是电梯自己的能力限制，加一个标志位并在 addRequest 里校验楼层最贴近这个约束，不用碰 Request。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming elevator capability into the request type would keep bloating Request with concerns unrelated to what a request actually means.
Swapping in a priority queue changes how movement gets ordered, which has nothing to do with which floors one elevator serves, and could disrupt SCAN.
The requirement is for both kinds of elevators to coexist — deleting regular ones leaves non-express floors unserved.
Express is really a capability limit on one elevator, so a flag plus a floor check inside addRequest matches that constraint without touching Request.

scenario: 想支持 priority floors 或 VIP，但仍希望保持平滑扫掠。
scenario_en: You want to support priority floors or VIP riders while keeping smooth SCAN-style movement.
q: 为什么直接用 priority queue 替代 SCAN 有风险？
q_en: Why is replacing SCAN with a priority queue risky?
options: 会打破沿方向扫掠，导致电梯跳来跳去
priority queue 不能存楼层
SCAN 不能处理优先级
VIP 一定不需要电梯
why: 优先级可能让电梯频繁改变方向，损害效率和体验。更稳的是让 dispatch 偏好特定电梯或在局部策略中权衡。
why_en: A priority queue can undermine the smooth sweep behavior that makes SCAN predictable.
options_en: It breaks the one-direction sweep, making the elevator jump around.
A priority queue cannot store floor numbers.
SCAN is fundamentally unable to handle priorities.
VIP passengers would never need an elevator at all.
tradeoff: priority queue 灵活抢占 vs SCAN 平滑扫掠的可预测性

termDefinitions.meaning: 按优先级取出元素的队列，不保证到达顺序或位置顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A priority queue pops elements by priority rather than arrival or positional order.

termDefinitions.fullName: Scan（电梯/磁盘扫描调度算法）
termDefinitions.meaning: SCAN 是沿当前方向持续服务请求、直到前方没有请求才反向的调度算法，借用了磁盘调度的思想。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SCAN keeps moving in the current direction serving requests, and only reverses once nothing remains ahead — the same idea used in disk-arm scheduling.

whenOtherWins: 如果需求是紧急呼叫必须抢占普通请求，可以用 priority queue，但要接受折返和饥饿风险。
optionExplanations: 一旦按优先级取请求，电梯可能为了高优先级楼层反复掉头，破坏 SCAN 原本的单向扫掠。
priority queue 存楼层号或 Request 对象都没有技术障碍。
SCAN 本身不排斥优先级，真正的风险在于它会打断扫掠顺序，不是完全不能兼容。
VIP 请求仍然需要坐电梯，只是希望被优先服务，这跟不需要电梯是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Once requests come out by priority, the elevator can reverse repeatedly chasing high-priority floors, breaking SCAN's one-direction sweep.
A priority queue has no trouble storing a floor number or a Request object at all.
SCAN itself isn't incompatible with priority — the real risk is that priority can interrupt the sweep order, not a hard technical block.
VIP riders still need the elevator; they just want to be served sooner, which is a different claim than not needing one at all.

scenario: 用户误按一个目的楼层按钮，想撤销。
scenario_en: A rider accidentally presses a destination floor button and wants to cancel it.
q: 最小扩展是什么？
q_en: What is the minimal extension?
options: 整个 ElevatorController 都要重建
加 removeRequest(request)，从 set 删除
把该电梯全部请求都清空
直接把 direction 强制设成 IDLE
why: 请求集合是电梯状态的事实来源，removeRequest 是 addRequest 的逆操作。step 算法无需大改。
why_en: Canceling a floor request can be the inverse of addRequest by removing it from the request set.
whenOtherWins: 真实电梯通常不允许撤销，因为按钮亮灯给其他乘客承诺了停靠；产品要求决定是否支持。
options_en: Rebuild the entire ElevatorController.
Add removeRequest(request), which deletes it from the set.
Clear every pending request on that elevator.
Force the elevator's direction to IDLE.
tradeoff: removeRequest 逆操作 vs 重建 Controller

termDefinitions.meaning: addRequest 的逆操作，把某个请求从集合中删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: removeRequest is the inverse of addRequest — it deletes a request from the set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

optionExplanations: 撤销一个按钮跟重建整个协调者的职责没有关系，改动范围过大。
requests 集合就是电梯状态的事实来源，加一个对称的 removeRequest 删除对应请求就是最小改动。
清空该电梯全部请求会连累其他乘客已经排队的目的地。
强制回到 IDLE 会让电梯忘掉自己还有其它没撤销的请求。
optionExplanations_en: Undoing one button press has nothing to do with rebuilding the whole coordinator — that's far too broad a change.
The requests set is the source of truth for elevator state, so a symmetric removeRequest that deletes just that entry is the minimal fix.
Clearing every request on that elevator would also wipe out other riders' destinations still waiting in the queue.
Forcing the elevator back to IDLE would make it forget any other requests it still legitimately has.

scenario: 多个 hall call 同时进入，且 step 正在遍历 requests。
scenario_en: Multiple hall calls can arrive while step is iterating through the requests set.
q: 最简单正确的并发方案是什么？
q_en: What is the simplest correct concurrency approach?
options: 只给 getCurrentFloor 这个读方法加锁
允许两个线程同时修改同一个 HashSet
同一把锁包住 requestElevator 和 step
只要把 Request 设计成不可变类就够
why: select+add 和 step 遍历/删除都接触共享状态，必须互斥。简单全局锁正确但并发度低。
why_en: A shared lock around request assignment and stepping prevents concurrent modification and selection races.
whenOtherWins: 更高并发可用线程安全队列收集请求，在每个 tick 开始时由 step drain 到 active set。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["requestElevator"] --> L["controller lock"]
  B["step"] --> L
  L --> C["assign or mutate requests"]
  C --> D["consistent elevator state"]
options_en: Only put a lock around the read-only getCurrentFloor.
Let two threads mutate the same HashSet concurrently.
Wrap requestElevator and step with the same lock.
Just make Request an immutable class and stop there.
tradeoff: 全局锁简单正确 vs 并发度低

termDefinitions.meaning: 互斥锁，保证同一时刻只有一个线程能进入被保护的代码段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock (mutex) ensures only one thread can enter the protected section at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于哈希表实现的集合，元素遍历顺序不保证稳定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A HashSet is a hash-table-backed set whose iteration order is not guaranteed to be stable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装一次停靠请求的类，包含楼层号和请求类型两个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Request object bundles a floor number together with a request type.

codeSample:
requestElevator(floor, type)
    lock.acquire()
    ... select + add ...
    lock.release()

step()
    lock.acquire()
    ... move + remove ...
    lock.release()
optionExplanations: 只给读方法上锁，挡不住选电梯和挪动电梯这些真正的写操作。
两个线程直接改同一个 HashSet 会触发数据竞争或遍历时抛异常。
选电梯这一步和电梯移动这一步都会读写同一份 requests 数据，只要用一把锁把两处调用都包起来，就不会互相踩踏。
让 Request 本身不可变确实有帮助，但 requests 这个集合仍会被并发增删，光靠不可变对象保护不了集合操作。
optionExplanations_en: Locking only a read-only method doesn't protect the actual writes happening in select+add or step.
Letting two threads mutate the same HashSet directly invites data races or iteration exceptions.
Picking an elevator and moving one both end up reading and writing the same requests data, so wrapping both call sites in one lock keeps them from stepping on each other.
Making Request immutable helps, but the requests collection itself is still concurrently added to and removed from, so immutability alone doesn't protect the collection operations.

scenario: 你想避免 hall call 在 step 执行时长时间阻塞。
scenario_en: You want to avoid blocking hall-call threads for the full duration of step.
q: 替代锁的更优雅方案是什么？
q_en: What is the cleaner alternative to locking?
options: 让 Controller 干脆忽略并发请求
每来一个请求就新建一个 Elevator
直接把 requests 这个 set 删掉不用
写入线程安全队列，step 时 drain 到 active set
why: 生产者只碰队列，step 只处理 active set，读写分离减少锁竞争。这个模式适合离散 tick 模拟。
why_en: A thread-safe pending queue lets producers enqueue while the step loop drains into active requests at tick boundaries.
whenOtherWins: 如果实现时间有限或并发很低，单锁方案更容易证明正确。
options_en: Have the controller simply ignore concurrent requests.
Spin up a brand-new Elevator for every incoming request.
Just delete the requests set entirely.
Write into a thread-safe queue and drain it into the active set at the start of each step.
tradeoff: 并发队列读写分离 vs 全局锁实现更简单

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持多线程并发读写且不产生数据竞争的队列，如 Java 的 BlockingQueue。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thread-safe queue supports concurrent reads and writes without data races, such as Java's BlockingQueue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互斥锁，保证同一时刻只有一个线程能进入被保护的代码段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock (mutex) ensures only one thread can enter the protected section at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

optionExplanations: 忽略并发请求会直接丢单，用户的 hall call 会消失。
每个请求都新建电梯会让电梯数量无限膨胀，跟固定 3 部电梯的题设矛盾。
删掉 requests 集合，step 就没有事实来源可读，整个状态机会失效。
生产者只写入线程安全队列，step 开始时统一 drain 到 active set 处理，读写分离让锁竞争降到最低。
optionExplanations_en: Ignoring concurrent requests just drops them silently — a rider's hall call would vanish.
Spinning up a new elevator per request makes the fleet grow without bound, contradicting the fixed-three-elevator setup.
Deleting the requests set leaves step with no source of truth to read, and the whole state machine stops working.
Producers just write into a thread-safe queue, and step drains it into the active set once at the start of each tick, separating reads from writes to minimize contention.

q: Elevator.step 必须处理哪些细节？（多选）
q_en: Which details must Elevator.step handle? (Select all that apply)
options: 无请求则 IDLE
IDLE 有请求时确定初始方向
停靠后本 tick 不移动
前方无请求时反向
why: 这些 edge cases 决定模拟是否稳定。漏掉任一项都可能导致漂移、不可复现或跳过停靠。
why_en: The step method must handle idle, initial direction, stop ticks, and reversal explicitly.
options_en: Go IDLE when there are no requests.
Pick an initial direction when IDLE but requests exist.
Do not move on the same tick it stops.
Reverse when nothing remains ahead in the current direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

optionExplanations: 漏了这一步，电梯没请求时会继续沿旧方向漂移，永远不停。
静止但有新请求时不显式选方向，第一步该往哪走就没有依据。
不显式 return 会让电梯在停靠的同一 tick 又移动一层，行为不自然。
前方清空却不反向，电梯会卡死在一端，永远接不到反方向的请求。
optionExplanations_en: Skip this and an elevator with no requests keeps drifting in its old direction forever.
Without explicitly picking a direction when idle but requests exist, there's no basis for which way the first move should go.
Without an explicit return, the elevator would move one more floor on the same tick it just stopped — an unnatural double action.
Failing to reverse once nothing remains ahead strands the elevator at one end, never able to serve the opposite direction.

q: 补全 Elevator 构造初始状态：
q_en: Fill in the initial state constructed for each Elevator:
text: 每部电梯初始在 {{0}} 楼，direction 为 {{IDLE}}，requests 是 {{空集合}}。
why: 题目给出固定 3 部电梯服务 0-9 层，构造时统一从 ground floor 开始。
why_en: Each elevator starts at floor zero, idle, with no pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

q: Controller 立即派发 hall call 而不是维护 pending 队列的取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the tradeoff of dispatching hall calls immediately instead of keeping a pending queue?
options: 更简单，但忙时不如队列灵活重派
一定比排队模型更公平地服务乘客
根本无法同时处理多个请求
必须依赖数据库才能实现
why: 立即派发让 Controller 状态少，只存 elevators。队列模型可在电梯空闲时重新选择，但实现更复杂。
why_en: Immediate dispatch keeps the controller simple, while a controller queue enables more flexible scheduling.
options_en: Simpler to build, but less flexible than a queue for re-dispatching when elevators are busy.
It is always fairer to passengers than a queuing model.
It cannot handle more than one request at a time.
It requires a database to work at all.
tradeoff: 立即派发实现简单 vs 忙时无法重新调度

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

optionExplanations: 把 hall call 直接分给一部电梯，Controller 只用记着 elevators 这一份状态，代价是电梯都忙时没法回头重新分配。
公平与否取决于调度策略本身，不是立即派发这个动作天然带来的，不能一概而论。
多个 hall call 依然可以逐个立即派发到不同电梯的队列，并不受限于同时只能处理一个。
这套设计完全可以用内存里的 elevators 列表实现，不需要数据库参与。
optionExplanations_en: Dispatching immediately means the controller only tracks the elevator list, simple to build, but it can't reconsider a bad pick once every elevator is already busy.
Fairness depends on the actual dispatch policy, not something that automatically comes from dispatching immediately — it's not a given.
Multiple hall calls can still be dispatched immediately, one after another, into different elevators' own queues, not limited to handling one at a time.
This whole design runs fine off an in-memory elevator list — a database isn't required at all.

scenario: 公司要把同一套电梯软件部署到不同建筑，有的重视等待时间，有的重视能耗。
scenario_en: The same elevator software will run in different buildings; some optimize wait time, others optimize energy.
q: 调度算法应如何扩展？
q_en: How should the dispatch algorithm be extended?
options: 给每栋建筑各复制一份 Controller 代码
抽出 SchedulingStrategy 接口供 Controller 组合
让 Elevator 自己猜测所在建筑类型
把 RequestType 直接改成字符串类型
why: 当选择电梯的策略确实要替换时，Strategy 才有价值。基础题不用先抽象。
why_en: Scheduling strategy becomes useful when different buildings genuinely need swappable dispatch policies.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有一种简单调度规则，直接写在 Controller 中更清楚。
options_en: Duplicate a whole copy of the Controller for every building.
Extract a SchedulingStrategy interface that the controller composes.
Have each Elevator guess what kind of building it's in.
Change RequestType into a plain string.
tradeoff: Strategy 接口可替换 vs 基础题直接写死

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可替换的算法各自封装成同一接口的实现，运行时可切换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Strategy pattern wraps interchangeable algorithms behind one common interface that can be swapped at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调度函数，按某种策略从多部电梯中选出最合适的一部。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: selectBestElevator is the dispatch function that picks the best elevator under a chosen strategy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

optionExplanations: 复制代码会让维护成本随建筑数量线性增长，每次改一处逻辑都要同步改所有副本。
把调度算法抽成 SchedulingStrategy 接口，让 Controller 组合持有，能在运行时换算法而不改 Controller 本身。
单部电梯拿不到、也不该拿到所在建筑类型这种全局信息，这是 Controller 层的事。
把枚举改成字符串会丢掉编译期类型安全，跟策略可替换性完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Duplicating the code makes maintenance cost grow with every building — one logic change now has to be repeated in every copy.
Extracting a SchedulingStrategy interface that the controller composes lets the algorithm be swapped at runtime without touching the controller itself.
A single elevator has no business knowing, or needing to know, which kind of building it's in — that's controller-level information.
Turning the enum into a plain string throws away compile-time type safety and has nothing to do with making the strategy swappable.

scenario: 电梯反向后当前楼层正好有反方向 pickup。
scenario_en: After an elevator reverses, the current floor may now have a pickup matching the new direction.
q: 为什么反向时 return，下一 tick 再检查停靠？
q_en: Why return after reversing and check stopping on the next tick?
options: 因为反向会让 requests 自动清空
因为反向这一步必须顺带移动一层
让新方向 shouldStopHere 能正确匹配
因为反向后 currentFloor 变得不可信
why: 反向改变了 pickupType。下一 tick 重新执行停靠检查，能服务当前楼层的反方向请求。
why_en: Returning after reversal lets the next tick evaluate stops at the same floor under the new direction.
options_en: Because reversing automatically empties the requests set.
Because reversing must also move the elevator one floor.
So the newly reversed direction's stop check can correctly match requests at the same floor.
Because currentFloor becomes untrustworthy after reversing.
tradeoff: 反向后 return 等下一 tick vs 同 tick 立即检查停靠

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断电梯是否该在当前楼层停靠的检查，只认同方向 pickup 或 destination。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: shouldStopHere decides whether to stop at the current floor, honoring only same-direction pickups or destinations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

whenOtherWins: 如果把停靠检查和反向检查合并成一次 tick 内的多步状态机，也能得到同样结果，但实现和调试都更复杂。
optionExplanations: 反向只是改变 direction 字段，requests 集合完全不受影响。
代码里反向后直接 return，明确不在同一 tick 里移动。
反向之后 pickupType 的含义也跟着变了，下一 tick 用新方向重新跑一次停靠检查，才能接住当前楼层刚好符合新方向的乘客。
currentFloor 是独立字段，反向不会让它变得不可靠。
optionExplanations_en: Reversing only flips the direction field — the requests set is completely unaffected.
The code returns right after reversing, deliberately not moving on that same tick.
Reversing flips what pickupType means, so the very next tick has to redo the stop check with the fresh direction — that's how it catches a rider at this floor who now matches.
currentFloor is an independent field; reversing direction doesn't make it any less trustworthy.

scenario: 仿真调用 controller.step()。
scenario_en: The simulation advances by calling controller.step().
q: Controller.step 应该做什么？
q_en: What should Controller.step do?
options: 重新构造所有电梯
自己移动所有电梯楼层并删除请求
只调度新请求不推进时间
遍历每部电梯调用 e.step()
why: Controller 推进整体时间，但运动细节由每个 Elevator 封装。这样 Controller 不需要知道 SCAN 的内部状态。
why_en: Controller.step advances time by asking each elevator to step itself.
options_en: Reconstruct every elevator from scratch.
Move every elevator's floor and remove requests itself.
Only dispatch new requests without advancing time.
Loop through every elevator and call e.step().
tradeoff: Controller 只推进时间 vs 直接操控电梯内部状态

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推进仿真一个离散时间单位的方法调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: step() advances the discrete-time simulation by one tick.

whenOtherWins: 如果需要跨电梯的全局约束（比如统一限速或动画帧同步），Controller 可以在遍历时附加逻辑，但单部电梯的移动算法仍应留在 Elevator.step 内部。
optionExplanations: 每 tick 重建电梯会丢掉它们当前的楼层、方向和请求这些运行状态。
让 Controller 亲自改楼层和删请求，会把本该封装在 Elevator 内部的移动细节泄漏出来。
只调度不推进时间，仿真的时钟就永远不会往前走。
Controller 只负责推进整体时间，具体怎么走、停、反向都交给每部电梯自己的 step 处理。
optionExplanations_en: Rebuilding every elevator each tick would throw away their live floor, direction, and request state.
Having the controller directly change floors and remove requests leaks movement details that should stay encapsulated inside Elevator.
Dispatching without advancing time would leave the simulation clock stuck forever.
The controller's job is just to advance overall time, leaving how each elevator moves, stops, or reverses to its own step method.

q: Senior 级回答应该主动说明哪些点？（多选）

options_en: The direction problem with floor-only requests.
The limits of nearest dispatch and the request-aware improvement.

optionExplanations: 说明白只存楼层号会丢掉方向，证明候选人理解请求身份建模。
主动指出 nearest 会派错方向的电梯，并给出 request-aware 的改进，展示从能跑到正确的推进过程。

scenario: 你要总结 Elevator.step 的核心不变量。
scenario_en: You need to summarize the core invariant of Elevator.step.
q: 哪个不变量最准确？
q_en: Which invariant is the most accurate?
options: 每 tick 最多一种动作：停靠/反向/移动/idle
每个 tick 都必须移动整整一层
每个请求进来都必须立刻被服务
电梯的方向永远保持不变
why: 离散模拟的清晰性来自每 tick 单动作。停靠和反向都不应再同 tick 移动。
why_en: A clear tick model lets an elevator do at most one action per step: stop, reverse, move one floor, or idle.
whenOtherWins: 如果仿真粒度更细，可把开门、关门、移动拆成更多状态。
options_en: Each tick performs at most one action: stop, reverse, move one floor, or idle.
Every tick must move the elevator exactly one floor.
Every incoming request must be served immediately.
The elevator's direction never changes.
tradeoff: 每 tick 单动作的清晰性 vs 一 tick 内多动作的复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

optionExplanations: 每个 tick 只做停靠、反向、移动或 idle 里的一件事，这个约束让整套模拟行为清晰、可推理。
停靠或反向的那个 tick 就不移动，每 tick 必须移动一层的说法跟代码实际行为矛盾。
请求进来后先排队等待电梯经过，不是立刻被服务，这不符合调度模型。
方向恰恰会随请求变化而反向，说它永远不变是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Each tick does exactly one of stop, reverse, move-one-floor, or idle — that single-action constraint is what keeps the whole simulation reasoning clear.
A tick spent stopping or reversing doesn't move at all, so claiming every tick must advance a floor contradicts the actual code.
An incoming request waits in the queue until an elevator passes it, not served the instant it arrives — that doesn't match the dispatch model.
Direction is exactly what flips as requests change; claiming it never changes is simply false.

q: 中级候选人在本题最应稳定实现哪部分？
q_en: What should a mid-level candidate implement reliably in this problem?
options: 完整真实电梯硬件控制
继续当前方向直到前方无请求再反向的状态机
分布式调度协议
乘客重量传感器
why: 中级重点是正确的 UP/DOWN/IDLE 转换、停靠不移动、请求清空转 idle。硬件细节不在范围内。
why_en: The expected mid-level core is a correct directional state machine for elevator movement.
options_en: Full real elevator hardware control.
A state machine that keeps its direction until nothing remains ahead, then reverses.
A distributed dispatch protocol.
Passenger weight sensors.
tradeoff: 中级：方向状态机 vs 高级功能（硬件/分布式）

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.fullName: Scan（电梯/磁盘扫描调度算法）
termDefinitions.meaning: SCAN 是沿当前方向持续服务请求、直到前方没有请求才反向的调度算法，借用了磁盘调度的思想。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SCAN keeps moving in the current direction serving requests, and only reverses once nothing remains ahead — the same idea used in disk-arm scheduling.

optionExplanations: 真实硬件控制超出了这道软件模拟题的范围，不是候选人要证明的能力。
候选人要把方向在 UP、DOWN 和 IDLE 之间怎么切换、什么时候不该移动、请求清空后怎么归位这套逻辑做对，这是这道题最基本也最该稳的部分。
这是单机 LLD 题，分布式调度协议属于更高阶的系统设计范畴。
载重和传感器属于硬件安全层，题目明确排除，不该在这里实现。
optionExplanations_en: Full real hardware control is outside this software-simulation problem's scope — it's not what the candidate needs to prove.
Getting the UP/DOWN/IDLE transitions right, not moving on a stop tick, and going idle once requests clear is the most basic thing this problem asks a candidate to nail.
This is a single-machine LLD problem — a distributed dispatch protocol belongs to a higher-level system-design question.
Weight sensors sit in the hardware-safety layer that this problem explicitly excludes; they shouldn't show up here.

scenario: 有人想让 Controller 直接读写每部电梯的 requests set 来实现移动。
scenario_en: Someone wants Controller to read and mutate each elevator requests set directly to implement movement.
q: 为什么不推荐？
q_en: Why is this design not recommended?
options: requests 不能删除
Controller 没有 elevators 列表
移动规则是单部电梯内部行为，应封装在 Elevator.step
Elevator 不应保存 currentFloor
why: Controller 的职责是协调和推进，不应知道电梯如何停靠、反向和移动。封装让移动算法可单独测试和替换。
why_en: Elevator.step should encapsulate movement rules so the controller stays a coordinator.
options_en: Requests inside the set cannot be removed.
The controller doesn't actually have a list of elevators.
Movement rules are a single elevator's internal behavior and belong inside Elevator.step.
Elevator should not store currentFloor at all.
tradeoff: 移动逻辑封装在 Elevator vs Controller 直接读写电梯状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

whenOtherWins: 如果未来要支持跨进程的分布式电梯集群，可能需要一个中间协调层读写共享状态，但单机设计里移动逻辑仍应封装在 Elevator。
optionExplanations: Set 里的元素完全可以删除，停靠动作本身就是一次 remove。
Controller 通常持有整个 fleet 列表，这不是它缺少的信息。
怎么停靠、反向、移动是单部电梯的内部行为，应该封装在 Elevator.step 里，让移动算法能单独测试和替换。
currentFloor 恰恰是 Elevator 最核心的一块状态，不存它电梯就不知道自己在哪。
optionExplanations_en: Elements in the set can absolutely be removed — a stop is literally a remove operation.
The controller typically holds the whole fleet list already, so that isn't information it's missing.
How to stop, reverse, and move is a single elevator's internal behavior that belongs inside Elevator.step, so the movement algorithm can be tested and swapped independently.
currentFloor is exactly the core piece of state an elevator needs — without it, it wouldn't know where it is.
